# Apple’s New iPad Mini Adds OLED, A20 Pro, and IP67 Water Resistance

 By Darryl Lara 4 min read Add us on

Imaging Resource is reader-supported. When you buy through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. How this works.

Apple has announced a redesigned iPad mini, bringing an OLED display, a thinner and lighter body, and a substantial performance upgrade to its smallest tablet. The new model features an 8.5-inch display, Apple’s A20 Pro chip, faster wireless connectivity, and IP67-rated water and dust resistance. [...] Apple is also offering an optional nano-texture display designed to reduce glare in bright environments. The feature could be particularly useful for photographers and other creatives editing images outdoors, as well as professionals working in the field.

The redesigned tablet measures just 5.4mm thick and is available in Midnight and Starlight finishes. It also carries an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance.

## A20 Pro Brings Faster Performance and On-Device AI

The iPad mini is powered by Apple’s A20 Pro chip, built using a 2-nanometer manufacturing process. The processor brings upgrades to graphics performance, everyday computing, and AI-intensive workloads. [...] The 12-megapixel Center Stage front camera has been repositioned to the landscape edge, making it better suited to video calls and conference meetings when the tablet is held horizontally.

Apple has also introduced an Acoustic Display system. Specially designed woofers work through the display to produce deeper bass and greater volume, while custom tweeters positioned between the glass and aluminum enclosure deliver clearer high frequencies. The sealed enclosure also helps the tablet achieve its IP67 rating.

# OLED iPad mini arrives with A20 Pro processor, better dust protection

AppleInsider

AppleInsider

edited 12:47PM   in iPad

It may not be able to fold, but the iPad mini 8 is the smallest tablet available that runs iPadOS. Here's what's new.

Tablet on a white table displaying a colorful pink and purple home screen with app icons and widgets, supported by a small stand, with a blurred brick wall background  
iPad mini 7 is revealed with OLED and A20 Pro chip [...] Another boon in the new model is the water and dust resistance rating of IP67. Apple didn't assign a rating on previous iPad minis, so this should take some pressure off use near bodies of water.  
  
However, that doesn't mean iPad mini will survive being in a shower or bathroom with steam. These ingress ratings are for at-rest liquid water, not steam or sprays, so be careful even with this rating.  
  
That said, a quick accidental dunk or spill shouldn't break the iPad mini.  
  
Networking specs have also seen a slight bump to Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, as well as Thread. If you're working with the latest accessories and routers, these specs will mean faster speeds and improved connectivity. [...] 1
 fred1

  fred1

  Apple states that: “iPad mini (A20 Pro) is splash, water, and dust resistant and was tested under controlled laboratory conditions with a rating of IP67 under IEC standard 60529 (maximum depth of 1 meter up to 30 minutes). Splash, water, and dust resistance are not permanent conditions. Resistance might decrease as a result of normal wear. Do not attempt to charge a wet iPad; refer to the user guide for cleaning and drying instructions. Liquid damage not covered under warranty.”  
    
   I think that means better water resistance than a steamy bathroom or a splash of water. At least that’s what Apple claims.
